The dog pins the attacker and growls, then returns to his small form. The man embraces him and says, "Thank you, buddy."

Real-time action, convincing weight, physical contact, momentum, and landings. No slow motion or speed ramps.

REFERENCES
image1 shows TWO FORMS OF THE SAME DOG, not two separate animals.

LEFT: the small normal Dalmatian.
RIGHT: his gigantic muscular transformed form.

Match the white fur, black spots, floppy spotted ears, canine face, two brown eyes, and pale-blue third eye centered on the forehead. Preserve recognizable markings between forms. The giant dog retains the reference's massive torso, thick limbs, enormous paws, and natural canine anatomy. No armor or additional limbs.

image2 defines the young adult man. Preserve his exact face, dark brown skin, short curly platinum-blond hair, pale eyes, pointed ears, and asymmetric horns. In the frontal reference, the black horn is on image-left and the ivory horn on image-right. Keep their anatomical placement consistent through camera changes.

Copy his layered ivory hooded robe, textured fabric, brown belt and pouch, leather forearm bindings, and brown boots. Hood down throughout.

These images define character appearance, not scenery. Do not reproduce the studio backgrounds.

REALISM
Live-action feature-film appearance. Natural skin pores, individual fur strands, worn leather, frayed cloth, splintered timber, and dusty stone.

Fantasy creatures have convincing muscle movement, grounded contact shadows, and substantial physical weight. Blue transformation fire illuminates nearby surfaces and airborne dust without burning the building or clothing.

Warm forest daylight outside; dim barn interior with sunlight entering gaps between boards and roof beams. Realistic motion blur and coherent exposure.

CHARACTERS
MAN: frightened but responsive. He retreats when threatened, moves clear of the fight, and approaches only after the attacker is subdued.

DOG: starts as the small Dalmatian from image1. His forehead eye glows blue before transformation. His giant form remains white with black spots and floppy ears. Its mass is comparable to the attacker's. He moves like a powerful quadrupedal animal.

ATTACKER: towering rat-like humanoid with a hunched muscular body, coarse gray-brown fur, long pinkish muzzle, rounded ears, uneven yellow teeth, heavy clawed hands, and a fleshy tail. His confidence becomes panic after the dog's transformation.

LOCATION AND GEOGRAPHY
An old timber-and-stone barn beside a forest clearing.

Tall double wooden doors form the ONLY entrance used in this sequence. They are closed and secured from inside with a heavy wooden crossbar seated in fixed frame brackets. The entire old doorway can break under the creatures' combined impact.

A stone grinding wheel stands to the left. Barrels line the right wall. Dust and grain cover the floor. A broad central lane connects the interior to the doors.

The man remains beside the right wall during the confrontation. The dog enters the central lane before transforming. The attacker retreats to the closed entrance.

Allow enough interior space for the giant dog to take two powerful strides and leap. The doorway is broad enough for both creatures to crash through as its doors and damaged frame break outward.

Outside, leave clear dirt ground for the landing and pin.

TIMELINE

00:00-00:02 | FORCED INSIDE
Exterior three-quarter wide shot, already in motion.

The man and small dog are stepping backward over the open threshold into the barn. The attacker stands directly in front of them, outside, facing into the building.

He advances with a threatening clawed-hand gesture, driving them farther inside. The man recoils; the dog retreats beside his boots. The attacker follows them across the threshold.

Clearly establish that he is forcing them into the barn.

00:02-00:05.5 | THE CLOSED EXIT
Cut to an interior wide view.

The man and dog move clear of the entrance toward the right wall. The attacker closes both door leaves and lowers the nearby crossbar into its frame brackets.

Show the fully closed, secured doors. Daylight is reduced to thin cracks. All three characters are now INSIDE.

00:05.5-00:09.5 | INTIMIDATION
The attacker turns from the entrance and approaches the man.

In a medium two-shot, he bends forward, exposes his teeth, and brings his muzzle close to the man's face. The man takes a short backward step and raises a forearm defensively.

While the attacker focuses on the man, the small Dalmatian moves away from the man's boots into the clear central lane. Briefly widen the framing to show this repositioning.

The dog plants all four paws and faces the attacker. Avoid prolonged staring or idle poses.

00:09.5-00:11.5 | BLUE-FIRE TRANSFORMATION
Low three-quarter view of the dog in the central lane, with the other characters still visible behind him.

His forehead eye flashes BLUE. Blue fire spreads rapidly across his spotted fur.

In one continuous transformation, his torso enlarges, shoulders broaden, legs thicken, and paws expand. He becomes the giant Dalmatian from image1.

His paws press into the dusty floor as his weight increases. Grain and dust shift beneath them. The flames contract into blue wisps and disappear.

The man presses toward the right wall, outside the dog's path. The attacker turns toward the transformation.

00:11.5-00:13.5 | PANIC
The giant dog lowers his head, exposes his teeth, and takes one heavy step toward the attacker.

Brief close-up of the attacker's widening eyes and collapsing confidence.

Return to a wider view. The attacker retreats toward the CLOSED doors, then turns to face them and grabs the crossbar.

The dog pivots into alignment with the central lane. The man's position remains safely to the right.

00:13.5-00:15.5 | FAILED ESCAPE
Interior side view.

The attacker frantically tries to lift the crossbar. One end catches in its bracket. The beam remains in place and the doors stay CLOSED.

He glances back, but keeps his body facing the doors.

Behind him, the dog lowers his body and bends his hind legs, preparing to spring. Establish a short clear run-up between the dog and the attacker's back.

IMPORTANT: the attacker has not opened the doors or escaped. Both creatures remain completely INSIDE the barn.

00:15.5-00:17.5 | LEAP THROUGH THE DOORS
Interior three-quarter wide shot showing the giant dog, the attacker, and the closed doorway together.

The dog takes two forceful strides, compresses his hind legs, and LAUNCHES OFF THE FLOOR.

His front paws reach forward and catch the attacker's shoulders as his heavy chest strikes the attacker's upper back. This is ONE airborne pounce, not a standing shove or a separate paw strike.

SHOW THE DOG LEAVING THE FLOOR AND MAKING CONTACT.

The dog's forward momentum drives the attacker chest-first into the closed wooden doors. The dog remains pressed against his back as they hit.

The doors splinter violently OUTWARD. The crossbar and old frame fittings fail, hinges tear from weathered wood, and broken boards fly into the clearing.

Both creatures burst through the doorway TOGETHER, traveling from the dark interior into the sunlit exterior. The attacker leads; the dog follows directly against him.

Keep the camera inside until the impact breaks the doors and their bodies begin crossing the threshold.

Then cut to an exterior side angle CONTINUING THE SAME MOVEMENT. The attacker hits the dirt first and rolls onto his back. The dog's front paws release his shoulders, reach the ground, and absorb the landing, followed by his hind paws.

Do not replay the pounce after the cut. Do not show either creature outside before the breakthrough.

00:17.5-00:20.5 | PINNED AND GROWLING
Exterior medium-wide view.

The attacker lies on his back and starts raising his shoulders. The dog steps in and places one massive forepaw against his upper chest, pushing his shoulders back onto the dirt.

The dog supports most of his weight on his other three legs. He restrains the attacker without crushing him.

He lowers his snarling muzzle close to the attacker's face and releases a deep, sustained, feral growl like a wild beast.

The attacker struggles briefly, then remains frightened and subdued. No bite, repeated blow, or dismemberment.

In the background, the man carefully exits through the shattered opening and stops beside the barn, near the dog's rear flank and safely away from the attacker's reach.

00:20.5-00:25 | THANK YOU, BUDDY
Keep the man, dog, and defeated attacker spatially connected in a medium-wide shot.

The dog removes his paw and turns toward the man. The attacker stays on the ground.

A brief envelope of BLUE FIRE wraps around the dog. He rapidly shrinks into the small three-eyed Dalmatian in less than one second. Show the continuous contraction, with his paws remaining grounded and his spotted coat preserved.

As the dog shrinks, the man begins crouching and opens his arms.

The small Dalmatian takes one or two steps into the man's embrace. The man wraps both arms around his shoulders and chest, holds him close, and says warmly:
"Thank you, buddy."

The damaged barn entrance remains visible behind them.

CAMERA AND SOUND
Use wide shots to establish geography and show the leap, collision, destruction, and landings. Use closer framing for intimidation, fear, and the final embrace.

Maintain the interior-to-exterior direction of travel. Cut on continuing motion without duplicating impacts.

Natural forest ambience, interior room reflections, boots, paws, heavy creature footfalls, wooden creaks, crossbar clunks, and breathing.

Blue fire creates a brief rushing flare. The breakthrough produces a sharp wood fracture, tearing fittings, scattering debris, and heavy ground impacts.

Foreground the dog's sustained wild-animal growl during the pin.

Only spoken dialogue:
"Thank you, buddy."

Clear English delivery and natural lip synchronization. No narration, added music, subtitles, logos, or end titles.

CONTINUITY
Exactly one man, one dog with two sequential forms, and one attacker. No cage or additional animal.

Both creatures are INSIDE immediately before the pounce. The attacker stands at the CLOSED doors with his back toward the dog.

The dog jumps onto the attacker. Their combined momentum breaks the doors OUTWARD. They cross the threshold together only after impact.

The exterior pin follows the visible landing. It is separate from the airborne pounce.

The man stays clear of the attack lane and exits only after the doorway has been destroyed.

The dog releases the attacker before shrinking. Both transformations use BLUE FIRE.

The attacker remains grounded during the reunion. Broken doors, damaged frame, scattered boards, and dust persist.

Preserve the man's reference identity, horns, and clothing, and the dog's three eyes, spotted coat, floppy ears, and reference anatomy.

No teleportation, duplicated animals, spontaneous armor, repaired doors, repeated completed actions, cartoon rendering, or plastic textures.

00–01  Already walking. Over my teammates' helmets, an @ Image 2 Obsidian stands on a plinth. The diagonal sunlight covers its body, but its ivory head, high above the beam, is in shadow. At the plinth's base lies a dropped @ Image 1 helmet from the missing first team.
01–02  As the leader passes beneath it, the @ Image 2 Obsidian's head slowly turns a full ninety degrees, following him. Its body stays frozen in the sunlight. No one else looks up.
02–03  The head turns further and stops facing straight into my goggles. I snap my rifle up at it.
03–04  The leader pushes my barrel down without looking up and signals forward. We cross through the doorway into the dark hall. Rifle lights snap on.

ACT 2 - THE HALL
04–05  My beam sweeps rows of plinths. Every plinth is empty.
05–06  A scrape from above. I tilt up.
06–07  Dozens of @ Image 2 Obsidians cling to the ceiling and pillars, all heads already turned toward us.
07–08  They drop. The nearest @ Image 2 Obsidian lands in my beam and glides straight at us on its coiling tendrils.
08–10  The machine gunner opens fire on my left. Muzzle flashes strobe the hall. Rounds dimple pale skin and sink in. The @ Image 2 Obsidians never flinch and come faster, flowing over each other across the floor and up the walls.
10–11  A tendril from the ceiling wraps the gunner's vest.
11–12  He is yanked straight up into the dark, still firing. His last flashes climb the wall and stop.
12–13  The leader grabs my shoulder and points back at the bright doorway. Retreat.

ACT 3 - THE RUN
13–15  I turn and sprint. The bright doorway bounces ahead. On both walls, @ Image 2 Obsidians race alongside us in the dark, keeping pace.
15–16  The rookie, running on my right, goes down hard. Floor tendrils of an @ Image 2 Obsidian have his boot.
16–17  He reaches an open glove toward mine. Our fingertips come within an inch.
17–18  His glove slips away. He slides feet first back into the dark.
18–20  Ten meters to the door. An @ Image 2 Obsidian lunges from the left. The leader shoves me forward with both hands.
20–21  I tumble through the doorway into the sunlight and land at the foot of the plinth. Behind me, tendrils wrap the leader and drag him back into the hall.

ACT 4 - THE LINE
21–22  I roll onto my back on the sunlit floor, rifle up, facing the doorway.
22–24  The whole swarm of @ Image 2 Obsidians surges to the doorway and stops dead where sunlight meets shadow. Tendril tips hover a hand's width from the light. Heads tilt. Only my breathing.
24–25  Hold on the frozen wall of ivory heads. My rifle lowers slightly.
25–26  The sunlight dims as a cloud crosses the skylight. The edge of the light slides back across the floor toward me.
26–27  As the shadow passes over them, the @ Image 2 Obsidians pour across the threshold.
27–28  Above me, the same @ Image 2 Obsidian from the plinth, now fully in shadow, bends down until its blank face is a hand's width from my goggles.
28–29  The seam at the base of its face parts, revealing two rows of tiny interlocking fangs.
29–30  It lunges. The view rolls sideways to tile level. A ribbed black tendril crosses the lens. Full black.

Use only sounds from the scene. Hear filtered breathing, boots on stone, tendrils scraping stone and ceiling, the wet rattle of many tendrils moving at once, gunfire and its echoes, the rookie's boot scraping away, the leader's muffled cry, sudden silence at the light line, and the final thud. No music, spoken lines or narration. Keep every human injury offscreen in darkness. No blood, HUD, subtitles, logos or reference-sheet graphics.

title: 完美的门口恶作剧（15 秒旧摄像机一镜到底）
author: @Mavern_0x
summary: 15 秒 9:16 老式磁带摄像机质感的家庭聚会恶作剧，一镜到底，真实感约束写得很细。
prompt:
15s / 1 continuous shot / vertical 9:16 / real live-action footage, real home video filmed on an old handheld tape camcorder by a friend

REALISM: This is real live-action footage filmed in real life, as if a real friend really recorded this prank at a house party on a real old tape camcorder. Not 3D, not CGI, not animation, not a render, not a video game, not cartoon, no plastic or glossy look. Soft standard definition tape video, interlaced motion with slight smear on fast action, light video noise in the shadows, mild compression blocking in dark corners, slight chroma bleed on the red and orange clothes, warm tungsten auto white balance, a small clipped highlight on the ceiling lamp. Real skin with pores and sweat shine, real cotton and fleece, real worn carpet fibers, real painted wood. Everything happens at real speed, no slow motion, no speed ramps.

STORY: At a house party a woman stands beside an open bedroom door and pranks her friends as they sprint down a long hallway into the room: at the last moment she swings the door half shut, each friend panics in a different hilarious way, she flings it open again and they fly through. Then the biggest friend charges, the floor shakes, she slams the door fully shut for real, and he blasts it off its hinges. She catches the falling door, it crashes down with him on top, he says he is okay, and then at the far end of the hallway an even bigger man appears and starts running.

SHOT LIST:
One continuous handheld take, no cuts.
0-2.5s: Friend 1 sprints, fake-out, flies through.
2.5-5s: Friend 2 fake-out, barrels into the camera.
5-7.5s: Friend 3 fake-out, slides across the carpet laughing.
7.5-10s: The floor shakes, the big friend charges, she slams the door fully shut.
10-12s: The door bursts into the room, she catches it, it crashes down with him on top.
12-15s: He groans he is okay, she laughs, then a second giant man appears in the hallway and runs.

SUBJECT:
The woman: around 30, fit athletic build, long dark wavy hair in a high ponytail that swings with every move, oval face, dark brows, brown eyes, natural skin with light freckles, no heavy makeup. Loose white oversized t-shirt, black biker shorts, grey socks. Mischievous grin, quick hands. Filmed like an ordinary friend, the camera never lingers on her body.
Friend 1: man around 22, slim, short black hair, bright green t-shirt, black joggers, white socks.
Friend 2: stocky man around 25, short black hair, all black hoodie and black sweatpants, white socks.
Friend 3: woman around 23, thin black framed glasses, curly brown hair, bright orange hoodie, black cargo pants, white socks.
The big friend: man around 25, by far the heaviest person, very wide round body, big belly, chubby cheeks, short curly black hair, black framed glasses, tight royal blue sweatshirt, bright red sweatpants, grey socks. Nearly as wide as the doorway.
The giant: man around 40, even taller and wider than the big friend, thick black beard, bald head, plain grey tank top, black shorts, bare forearms, grey socks. Appears only at the far end of the hallway after 13.5s.
Everyone is in socks, no shoes. The same people in every moment, nothing about their faces, hair, glasses, clothes or body size changes. Only one of each person exists at any time.

WORLD: A small bedroom with dark burgundy carpet, white walls, a white ceiling with one round warm ceiling lamp that stays on at the same brightness the whole time. On the right wall a small white shelf at shoulder height with a clear glass of water and two small framed photos with no visible text. The doorway is in the back wall. The door is a real white hollow core interior door, about 80 cm wide and 2 m tall, three brass hinges on its LEFT edge, a round brass knob. It opens INWARD and when fully open lies flat against the back wall LEFT of the doorway, right beside the woman. Through the doorway a straight bright beige hallway about 6 meters long ends in a white wall with one wide horizontal band of red and blue zigzag chevrons at mid height. The hallway is lit brighter than the room. Palette: burgundy, warm white, beige, with the red and blue chevrons as the accent.

LOOK: Camcorder held at chest height by a friend standing inside the room about 4.5 meters from the doorway, slightly LEFT of its center line, angled a little right toward it. Wide framing: ceiling and lamp at top, the woman's full body including feet on the left, the doorway and the whole hallway in the center, a wide area of carpet in the foreground, the shelf on the right wall. Constant hand shake and breathing sway, horizon slightly tilted, autofocus lags and snaps late onto each runner, two small clumsy zoom nudges that never push the doorway or a landing out of frame. Locked exposure, brightness never changes. No date stamp, no REC icon, no viewfinder overlay, the operator is never seen.

MOTION: Every run has a visible acceleration from the far wall, socks pushing off the floor, arms pumping. Each fright happens at real speed in under half a second: the body jerks back, knees buckle, arms fly up. Each jump has a crouch and push off one foot just before the threshold, a real arc of about 0.4 seconds and a landing where knees or feet touch the carpet first and the body weight follows. The big friend moves with heavy inertia: deep booming steps, belly and cheeks bouncing with each stride, shoulder lowered, he cannot slow down. The door swings only around its left hinges, has weight, rattles in its frame when slammed and never bends. The woman shifts her weight between her feet, her ponytail swings after every pull. The operator's hands shake harder when he laughs and jerk at the impact.

SHOTS IN DETAIL:
0-2.5s: The woman stands just left of the doorway, back near the wall, right hand on the inner knob, the door fully open flat against the wall beside her, the doorway completely clear. She glances at the camera with a sly grin, knees bent. Friend 1 sprints from the far end of the hallway, growing larger. At 1.3s, with him about 30 cm from the threshold, she swings the door to 45 degrees in front of him with a sharp whoosh. Friend 1, the stop sign: both palms thrust out, fingers spread, face clenched, teeth bared, eyes squeezed, knees knocking, body jerking back. Friend 1 screams: "Nooo!" At 1.6s she flings the door flat against the wall again and he flies through frozen in that pose, knees tucked, lands on both knees on the carpet right of center, slides forward with a carpet hiss and scrambles out of frame right. She snorts with laughter. <padded sock steps> <door whoosh> <knees thud on carpet>
2.5-5s: Friend 2 already runs heavily down the hallway, hood bouncing. The woman crouches lower, eyes locked on him. At 3.7s, 30 cm from the threshold, the door swings to 45 degrees. Friend 2, the karate block: one palm out, the other forearm across his chest, one knee jerked up, mouth wide open, eyebrows high, body twisting sideways. Friend 2 yells: "WHOA!" At 4.0s she flings the door open and he barrels through sideways, lands, staggers, cannot stop and runs straight at the camera. His black hoodie fills the lens, the camera jerks back, the image goes almost black for about 6 frames, he passes right of the camera and is gone. The camera re-centers, the operator laughing loudly. <heavy thud> <camcorder bump>
5-7.5s: Friend 3 sprints in already giggling, glasses bouncing. At 6.3s, 30 cm from the threshold, the door swings to 45 degrees. Friend 3, the laughing scaredy cat: a squeak, both hands fly to her cheeks, glasses crooked, knees buckle, then a huge squealing laugh, eyes squeezed into crescents. Friend 3: "Eeeek!" At 6.6s the door flies open and she hops through, lands, her socks slip, she stumbles two steps, sits down hard and rolls onto her back on the right side of the carpet, legs kicking, laughing. She stays there until 15s.
7.5-10s: Deep booming footsteps start in the hallway before anyone is clearly seen. The glass of water on the right shelf ripples in rings with each boom, the two photo frames tap against the wall. The woman's grin widens, she looks at the shelf, then down the hallway. The big friend charges at full speed, face fiercely determined, shoulder lowered, belly bouncing, cheeks shaking. The big friend gives a deep grunt. At 9.4s, while he is still about 1.5 meters from the threshold, she swings the door all the way shut with both hands, the latch clicks, the hallway disappears behind white wood. She lets go, takes one quick step forward and left into the room, raises both hands with a smug grin. She shows no fear yet. <booming steps getting louder> <glass rattling> <latch click>
10-12s: At 10.0s a huge hollow crash. The hinges and latch tear out of the frame, splinters fly, screws ping, the whole door bursts into the room as one panel, its top tipping forward and left toward the woman. On reflex she grabs its top edge with both hands and holds it tilted at about 45 degrees, arms straining, eyes huge. Behind it the big friend has dropped to one knee in the doorway, both palms pushing on the door, face strained. At 11.0s his weight wins, the door slips from her hands and slams flat onto the carpet, he falls forward on top of it, the hollow door cracks into several flat slabs with torn cardboard honeycomb inside. He lies face down on the slabs, never under them. The camera flinches hard. <crash that overloads the mic> <flat heavy slam> <splinters tapping carpet>
12-15s: The doorway is empty with torn wood at the hinge marks, the hallway and the chevron wall visible again. Friend 3 sits up on the right, mouth open. The big friend lifts his head and pushes up on his elbows, unhurt and dazed, glasses crooked. The big friend, groaning: "I'm okay..." The woman stands frozen, one hand pressed over her mouth, then bends forward in helpless laughter. The woman, gasping through her hand: "Oh my God!" At 13.5s, at the far end of the hallway, the giant steps out from the right side, looks straight down the hallway into the room, and starts to run toward it with heavy booming steps. The glass on the shelf starts rippling again. The woman's laugh cuts off, she straightens, looks at the empty doorway, then straight into the camera, eyes wide. The woman, quietly: "Oh no." The giant is still in the far half of the hallway, growing larger, as the video ends at 15.0s.

HARD MOMENTS:
1.3-1.6s, 3.7-4.0s, 6.3-6.6s RISK: the door touches a runner or bends. The door swings from flat against the wall to exactly 45 degrees and stops, its free edge about 40 cm in front of the runner, then swings straight back flat against the wall before the runner reaches the threshold. Each runner freezes in a pose for a split second and then is carried forward through the clear doorway by momentum. MUST NOT: door passing through a body, door bending, door held half shut while a runner is still far away, runner skidding to a full stop.
Each landing RISK: floating or weightless landing. Knees or feet hit the carpet first, the carpet dents, the body weight follows half a beat later, hair and clothes keep moving after the landing. MUST NOT: sliding feet without friction, extra limbs, morphing hands, glasses disappearing.
9.4-10.0s RISK: the big friend passing through the closed door. From 9.4s to 10.0s the door is fully shut and latched, the hallway hidden, nothing comes through it. Only at 10.0s does the whole panel break loose from its hinges as one solid flat piece. MUST NOT: body passing through wood, door opening the wrong way, door changing size or color.
10.0-11.0s RISK: the held door morphing. The woman holds the top edge with both hands, five fingers on each, the door a rigid flat rectangle tilted at 45 degrees, the brass knob still on it. Her arms shake under the weight, her heels dig into the carpet. MUST NOT: door bending like rubber, hands merging into wood, the door shrinking.
13.5-15s RISK: the giant duplicating the big friend. The big friend stays lying on the broken door in the room. The giant is a different man (beard, bald, grey tank top) and exists only in the far half of the hallway, never reaching the doorway before the end.

CONTINUITY: The door only swings on its left hinges and is fully open flat against the wall during every run 1 to 3. From 9.4s to 10.0s it is shut and latched. After 10.0s it is off its hinges, held tilted until 11.0s, then lies broken in slabs until 15s, and the doorway stays empty. Friends 1 and 2 leave frame and never return. Friend 3 stays on the right side of the carpet from 7s to the end. The big friend is never in the room before 10.0s and stays on the broken door after 11.0s. The lamp stays on at the same warm brightness the whole time.

AUDIO: All sound recorded by the camcorder's built in mic in a small carpeted room. Real human voices with breathy, uneven delivery, shouts that clip the cheap mic, panting, overlapping laughter. The woman has a warm natural American voice. The operator laughs loudly close to the mic. Padded sock steps, door whooshes, latch click, booming heavy steps, the rattling glass, a huge hollow wooden crash that briefly overloads the mic, the flat slam of the door on the floor, splinters tapping. No music, no narrator, no sound effects that sound like a cartoon.

KEEP: Five natural fingers on each hand. The door keeps the same size, color and three left hinges, and never reassembles after breaking. No blood or injury, everyone gets up or moves after falling. No extra people beyond the six described, no duplicates. No text, subtitles, timestamps, logos or camcorder UI. No cuts, no slow motion, no freeze frames, no light dimming. Real live-action footage filmed in real life. Not 3D, not CGI, not animation, not a render, not a video game, not cartoon, no plastic or glossy look.

FORMAT: 20 seconds, 9:16 vertical, photorealistic live-action medieval action blockbuster, 5 shots with hard cuts on action, fast brutal rhythm, three short slow-motion moments on the biggest hits, large-scale practical fire and destruction effects.

CINEMATIC QUALITY (mandatory, applies to every shot of this video):
Generate this video as real live-action footage from a top-budget feature film. It must be indistinguishable from a real camera shoot and never look AI-generated, CGI-plastic or animated. Shot on ARRI Alexa 65 with sharp high-end prime lenses, cinematography in the style of Greig Fraser: motivated natural light, soft realistic shadows, true-to-life exposure, deep but detailed blacks, no blown highlights. 24 fps with natural 180-degree shutter motion blur on all movement. Native high resolution with razor-sharp focus on the subject, crisp micro-contrast and high-frequency detail on every edge, skin pore and surface texture. Subtle organic film-like grain over the whole image, stable across frames. Natural, slightly muted real-world color grade with accurate skin tones. Keep this quality consistent from the first frame to the last, with no flicker, morphing, warping or texture shimmer.

CREATURE & LOOK QUALITY (applies to every shot):
Both gorillas must look like real living animals filmed on set, top-tier feature-film creature realism. Fur rendered strand by strand: coarse hairs with natural clumping, flyaways catching firelight, fur that reacts to every movement, wind and impact with correct weight and delay. Faces have deep wrinkles, pores, scars and fine hair on leathery skin, soft subsurface scattering in ears, lips and fingers. Eyes wet and alive, sharp catchlights, natural blinking. Readable facial performance: brow tension, bared teeth, flaring nostrils, heaving chest. Hands with leathery palms and knuckle creases gripping weapons with real pressure. Close-ups on long lenses with shallow depth of field and creamy bokeh, focus on the eyes. Air full of floating embers, smoke haze and ash catching the light. Muted earthy palette with deep shadows, warm amber firelight against cold blue night. No plastic skin, no waxy fur, no game-engine look.

REFERENCES: If photos are attached, they define the exact look of SIR BRUTUS, the BERSERKER and the courtyard. Keep them identical in every shot.

REALISM: Real gorilla anatomy and strength: massive shoulders, long arms, low wide stances, heavy weight shifts, knuckles touching the ground when they lunge. Every strike has four visible phases: wind-up, swing, one clear contact, consequence. Every impact transfers force: bodies slide, feet scrape and dig into cobblestones, stone cracks, wood splinters, metal dents and throws sparks, fur and cloak whip from the shock.
EFFECTS RULES: All effects look like real practical effects filmed on set. Fire is real burning tar and wood: thick orange flames, black smoke, flying embers, heat distortion, real moving firelight on fur, steel and stone. The burning hammer leaves a short trail of flame and sparks on every swing and never goes out. Sparks bounce and die on the wet ground. Debris falls with real weight. Water hitting fire turns into dense white steam with a loud hiss. Every effect comes from a visible physical cause.
SLOW MOTION RULES: Only three slow-motion moments, each about 1 second, ramping smoothly from real speed into slow motion just before contact and back to real speed right after: the first hammer impact on the shield (4.8s), the disarm (12.5s), the final shield strike (16.5s). In slow motion every spark, ember, water droplet, fur strand and splinter is sharp and visible.

CHARACTERS (both stay consistent in every shot):
- SIR BRUTUS: big muscular black-furred gorilla in polished but battle-scratched steel plate armor, OPEN-FACE steel helmet with a tall red feather plume, his whole gorilla face always fully visible. A round steel-rimmed wooden shield on his left arm, a longsword in a scabbard on his hip that he never draws. Fights calm, precise and defensive, using the shield as a weapon.
- BERSERKER: an even bigger scarred old silverback gorilla, bare chest and arms covered in thick fur, ragged black wolf-fur cloak, iron arm bracers, a huge two-handed iron war hammer with a long wooden handle, its head wrapped in tar-soaked rags. One white scar across his left eye. Fights wild, furious and with full power.

ENVIRONMENT: A medieval castle courtyard at night after a siege, fixed layout in every shot: wet cobblestone ground with puddles, a large iron fire brazier burning in the foreground left, a wooden cart in the foreground right, a stack of wooden wine barrels against the right wall, tall wooden scaffolding burning along the back wall held by thick wooden support posts, a long stone horse trough filled with water on the far left. Flickering warm orange firelight, cold blue moonlight from above, embers and ash drifting constantly, smoke haze.

TIMELINE:
SHOT 1 (0.0-3.5s), wide low angle on 35mm, camera near the ground behind puddles that reflect the fire, slow push-in:
0.0-1.0s: The BERSERKER plunges the rag-wrapped head of his hammer into the burning brazier. It ignites with a roaring whoosh, flames climb up the rags, firelight explodes across his face, burning drops of tar fall and sizzle in a puddle, his scarred eye narrows.
1.0-2.2s: He lifts the blazing hammer high with both hands and brings it down on the wooden cart. The cart explodes into a fireball of burning splinters and sparks, a wheel rolls away burning, splinters land and keep smoldering on the wet stones, the shockwave ruffles his cloak.
2.2-3.5s: He points the hammer at SIR BRUTUS across the courtyard and roars: "Kneel!" SIR BRUTUS lowers his stance, raises the shield, steam from his breath, and answers quietly: "Never."
SHOT 2 (3.5-7.5s), handheld medium shot on 50mm from the side, both fighters full in frame from head to knees:
3.5-4.5s: The BERSERKER charges, four heavy strides, puddles splashing, then raises the flaming hammer over his head with both arms fully extended. SIR BRUTUS plants his feet wide, left foot forward, bends his knees and lifts the shield above his head, angled slightly, braced with his shoulder and right hand on the rim.
4.5-5.5s (slow motion): The hammer comes down. Single clear contact on the center of the shield. A ring-shaped shockwave of fire, sparks and puddle water blasts outward along the ground, the plume and fur whip back, burning rag fibers and embers spray off the hammer head, the shield dents inward and scorches black, the shock ripples visibly through Brutus's arms and armor plates.
5.5-7.5s (real speed): SIR BRUTUS is driven down onto one knee and slides one meter back on the wet stones, cobblestones cracking under his knee. His teeth are clenched, veins visible under the fur of his forearm. He shoves the hammer off sideways with the shield, the hammer head scraping off the rim with sparks, and rises back to his feet.
SHOT 3 (7.5-11.0s), wide locked shot on 35mm showing both fighters full-body and the whole scaffolding behind them:
7.5-8.5s: The BERSERKER pulls the hammer back over his right shoulder and swings it horizontally at head height with a trail of flame, his whole torso rotating, feet pivoting on the stones.
8.5-9.3s: SIR BRUTUS ducks low under it, the flame passing inches over his plume. The hammer misses and smashes through a thick support post of the burning scaffolding behind him, wood exploding into burning chunks, the post snapping in two.
9.3-11.0s: The scaffolding groans and starts collapsing in sections, burning beams crashing onto the cobblestones in bursts of embers, a wall of sparks rising behind them. In the same moment SIR BRUTUS springs up from the crouch and drives the steel rim of his shield upward into the BERSERKER's jaw. His head snaps back, spit and sweat fly, he stumbles two steps back, shaking his head, a burning beam crashing down between them a moment later.
SHOT 4 (11.0-15.0s), handheld medium close shot on 50mm, debris and embers still falling in the background:
11.0-12.3s: The furious BERSERKER roars and swings the flaming hammer in a wide diagonal arc from high left to low right, stepping over the fallen burning beam, fire reflecting in his bared teeth.
12.3-13.3s (slow motion): SIR BRUTUS steps inside the arc, catches the wooden handle with the edge of his shield, locks it against his armored forearm and twists his whole body. The hammer is ripped out of the BERSERKER's hands, flames spiraling around it, the BERSERKER's hands sliding off the handle and his body thrown off balance by his own momentum.
13.3-15.0s (real speed): The flaming hammer flies across the courtyard and smashes into the wine barrels. They burst in a spray of dark wine, splinters and fire. Wine soaks the stones and catches small flickering flames around the barrels. The hammer lies there burning. The BERSERKER stares at his empty hands, then at SIR BRUTUS, nostrils flaring, rage building.
SHOT 5 (15.0-20.0s), low heroic angle on 35mm from behind SIR BRUTUS's shoulder, then the push-in finishes in front of him:
15.0-16.3s: The BERSERKER beats his chest with both fists and charges bare-handed through falling embers, roaring. SIR BRUTUS plants his feet, turns his hips and draws the shield back over his right shoulder, holding it with both hands by the rim.
16.3-17.3s (slow motion): He swings the shield in a full horizontal arc. Single clear contact on the side of the BERSERKER's head with a deep metallic boom. A dust and ember shockwave ripples outward, the BERSERKER's eyes roll, fur and skin on his face ripple from the impact, the shield rim bending slightly, sweat and water droplets frozen in the air.
17.3-18.5s (real speed): The BERSERKER is knocked off his feet and falls backward into the stone horse trough. A huge wave of water splashes over the nearby fire and explodes into a dense white steam cloud with a loud hiss. Water keeps pouring over the trough edges. He lies in the trough dazed, conscious, arms hanging over the sides, not moving.
18.5-20.0s: SIR BRUTUS stands among the flames and steam, beats his armored chest twice with his fist and lets out a powerful roar, as the last section of the scaffolding collapses behind him in a towering curtain of sparks. Steam and embers swirl around his silhouette, firelight flickers across his scorched shield and his face. Final frame: his face in close focus, breathing heavily, eyes calm. Hold until the end.

LIGHTING: Fire is always the motivated key light, flickering warm orange from the brazier, burning scaffolding and hammer. Cold blue moonlight is the rim light on fur and steel edges. Each explosion of fire briefly brightens faces and surroundings, then settles. Steam and smoke catch both lights and glow.

CAMERA: Shots 1 and 3 wide to show full bodies, space and the collapse. Shots 2 and 4 handheld, close to the action, camera reacting to impacts with a short real shake. Shot 5 low heroic angle. Cut on action only. Every contact is fully visible in frame, never hidden by a cut and never repeated from another angle.

AUDIO & DIALOGUE:
VOICE: Real human voice actors recorded in a studio, never synthetic, robotic or text-to-speech, with natural breath and imperfect real delivery, perfectly lip-synced to the gorilla mouths. All dialogue in English, only two lines: the BERSERKER (2.5s): "Kneel!" in a huge raw growling roar that echoes off the walls. SIR BRUTUS (3.0s): "Never." low, calm, deadly quiet. All other vocals are real primal gorilla roars, grunts of effort, chest beats and heavy breathing.
SOUND EFFECTS (mixed like a feature film in Dolby Atmos, real stone reverb): roaring whoosh of the hammer igniting, fireball explosion of the cart, splashing heavy footsteps, deep flaming whoosh on every swing, massive metallic clang with fire blast on the shield, cracking stone, groaning and snapping scaffolding, burning beams crashing, wrenching metal and wood on the disarm, barrels bursting, deep boom of the final shield strike, huge splash and violent steam hiss, crackling fires. In slow motion the sound drops into a low muffled rumble with a heartbeat, then slams back to full volume on the impact.
MUSIC (live orchestra, real musicians, epic action film score):
- 0.0-2.2s: low droning cellos and a single deep taiko hit on the cart explosion.
- 2.2-3.5s: music drops to silence under "Kneel!" and "Never."
- 3.5-4.5s: war drums and staccato strings explode with the charge.
- 4.5-5.5s: everything cuts to silence in slow motion, then a massive orchestral hit on the hammer impact.
- 5.5-11.0s: driving taiko, low brass and male choir, building with the scaffolding collapse.
- 11.0-15.0s: drums keep driving, a big brass stab exactly on the disarm at 12.5s, low strings under the BERSERKER's stare.
- 15.0-16.3s: drums accelerate with the final charge, choir rising.
- 16.3-17.3s: silence in slow motion, then the biggest choir and drum hit of the video on the final strike.
- 18.5-20.0s: a triumphant brass theme under Brutus's roar, fading into crackling fire.
Music never covers the dialogue or the key impacts.

CONTINUITY: The hammer burns from 1.0s until the end. The cart stays destroyed after 2.0s. The shield stays dented and scorched after 5.0s. The scaffolding keeps collapsing after 9.3s and fallen beams keep burning on the ground. After 13.5s the hammer lies burning by the smashed barrels and the BERSERKER is bare-handed. The BERSERKER stays in the trough after 17.5s. SIR BRUTUS keeps his open-face helmet, plume and shield the whole video and never draws the sword.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS: No closed helmet, no hidden face, no human characters, no extra characters, no cartoon or animated look, no text, no subtitles, no logos. No blood, no gore. No extra limbs, no morphing, no weapon appearing or disappearing, no location change between shots, no repeated hits, no slow motion outside the three listed moments.

title: 零秒之战：冻结时间的导弹（15 秒）
author: @DeCat2025
summary: 飞行员在时间冻结中改写导弹轨道，击毁指挥泰坦；5 个分镜，附音频与限制。
prompt:
Ultra-photorealistic Hollywood sci-fi action, premium live-action cinematography, enormous physical scale, intense combat and realistic destruction. A devastated futuristic battlefield at dusk. One special-forces pilot wears a distinctive matte-black armored time-displacement suit with thin cyan energy conduits. Directly ahead stands one enormous enemy command titan, an angular black mechanical war machine with a glowing red chest reactor and shoulder-mounted missile batteries.

SHOT 1 | 0–3s | LOW TRACKING ANGLE
The armored pilot charges through the broken remains of a concrete defensive barrier as the command titan unleashes a massive missile volley. Explosions rip across the battlefield. The pilot activates the suit with a sharp cyan energy flash just before the incoming missiles arrive.

SHOT 2 | 3–6s | HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE
Time freezes abruptly. Hundreds of missiles hang motionless above the battlefield, their exhaust flames suspended in midair. Debris and shockwaves become perfectly still. The pilot alone moves through the frozen destruction, heading directly toward one large missile aimed at the destroyed barrier.

SHOT 3 | 6–9s | MISSILE-LEVEL SIDE ANGLE
The pilot reaches the suspended missile and clamps a magnetic steering device onto its guidance assembly. The device rotates the missile's nose toward the titan's exposed red chest reactor. Cyan electrical fractures spread through the frozen air as the unstable time field begins collapsing.

SHOT 4 | 9–12s | EXTREME LOW ANGLE
Time resumes violently. The redirected missile accelerates into the command titan's chest reactor. A massive explosion tears open its frontal armor. The titan recoils under the impact, its giant mechanical legs buckle, and its upper body crashes backward into the battlefield, sending a wall of dust and wreckage outward.

SHOT 5 | 12–15s | FIXED GROUND-LEVEL WIDE ANGLE
The pilot stands in the foreground facing the fallen command titan. The titan's shattered chest burns behind the pilot as its last red reactor light goes dark. Fragments finish falling by 13 seconds. Smoke drifts across the ruined battlefield. Hold this completed cinematic composition unchanged for the final two seconds.

AUDIO:
Deafening missile launches, heavy mechanical cannon fire, thunderous explosions, sharp cyan time-activation pulse, sudden complete silence during frozen time, violent return of battlefield sound, deep metal collapse, final low-frequency cinematic rumble. No dialogue or narration.

CONTINUITY:
Exactly one pilot and one enemy command titan. Maintain the pilot's matte-black armor and cyan suit lights. Maintain the titan's black angular design, red reactor and exact location. The missile the pilot redirects must be the same missile that strikes the titan. One continuous battlefield, consistent screen direction, physical cause and effect, realistic mass and momentum.

RESTRICTIONS:
No extra pilots or titans, no duplicated body parts, no teleporting objects, no character or vehicle redesign, no arbitrary camera drift, no zoom-out, no face close-ups, no graphic injuries, no recognizable celebrity faces or public-figure likenesses. No unfinished final action.

Keep proportions. Keep style and features. Ratio 16:9.

title: 过山车假发倒带（30 秒一镜到底）
author: @ZDuo_MoreAi
summary: 过山车上假发飞出、时间冻结再精准倒带的 30 秒一镜到底，分段时间轴写得很清楚。
prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic daytime amusement park roller coaster, bright hard sunlight, strong wind, realistic motion blur on tracks and background, subtle handheld camera energy, rich skin detail, heavy natural film grain.
0-5s: [Medium Shot] A young woman in her early 20s sits in the front seat of a moving roller coaster car, calm and slightly bored, hair whipping in the wind. Beside her sits a middle-aged man wearing what looks like a normal full head of hair. Behind them, another car with a woman is visible. The coaster drops and banks hard.
5-9s: [Dynamic Tracking] The force of the turn rips the man's wig free. It peels off his bald head in a chaotic upward arc, spinning and flying backward through the air. The wig lands messily on the head of the woman in the car behind. Everyone's faces freeze in pure shock and confusion at the peak of the chaos. Time locks completely. Only the young woman in the front keeps moving.
9-15s: [Slow Orbital + Detail] Camera slowly orbits the frozen cars. The wig hangs mid-air in a twisted shape with individual hairs suspended. The bald man's scalp is fully exposed, mouth open. The woman behind is frozen mid-scream with the wig draped over her face. The young woman looks sideways, rolls her eyes and mouths "joder, otra vez". She reaches into her pocket, pulls out a stick of chewing gum, unwraps it and calmly puts it in her mouth, starting to chew while the entire frozen scene (except her) begins a precise reverse.
15-20s: [Medium Close-up] The rewind is controlled and elegant: the wig lifts off the woman behind, flies backward through the air in reverse, and returns exactly to the moment it is only beginning to peel off the bald man's head. Time freezes again at that precise instant — the front edge of the wig just lifting, a few strands already loose.
20-26s: [Tight Medium] Still frozen for everyone else, the young woman takes the chewed gum out of her mouth, reaches over and firmly presses it onto the center of the bald man's scalp, right under the lifting wig. With the same hand she smooths and presses the wig back down into perfect place, locking it with the gum. She sits back, looks straight ahead with a tiny private smile, completely unbothered.
26-30s: [Medium Shot] Time suddenly resumes at full real-time speed. The coaster continues its drop. The man touches his head, feels the wig still firmly in place, looks confused for a second, then breaks into a relieved, happy smile. The young woman stares forward, already chewing a new piece of gum, expression of quiet satisfaction.
Photorealistic, ultra-detailed wind and hair physics, perfect motion blur only on moving elements, stable characters, cinematic lighting, heavy natural film grain, no artifacts, movie-level temporal coherence, high rewatch value.

Photorealistic action, fluid choreography, precise martial-arts timing, visible blind eyes, stable character continuity, elegant speed ramps, readable combat geography, realistic body mechanics, subtle time-bending feel, no gore, normal proportions without stretch.

title: 迈阿密警察拦下美人鱼低底盘车（20 秒执法记录仪）
author: @devgetsit
summary: 9:16 执法记录仪视角的荒诞喜剧，角色与音效描述详细。
prompt:
Realistic police body camera footage, vertical 9:16, 20 seconds: chest-mounted camera with a wide fisheye lens and barrel distortion, slightly washed-out colors, low-light digital noise, the image bouncing with the officer's steps and breathing, one continuous take, no cuts. Night traffic stop on a Miami street: red and blue police lights flash across everything, the officer's harsh flashlight beam lights the faces. Funny, played completely straight. No guns, no weapons drawn, no on-screen text, no logos.

The creatures: three real mermaids in a red vintage lowrider convertible, top down, whose cabin is filled to the brim with water. All three sit side by side on the front bench seat, in the water up to their chests. Their shimmering fish tails stick out of the car and slap the car body the whole video: the driver's tail over the driver's door, the passenger's tail over the passenger door, the middle one's tail over the back of the seat. All three are glamorous Miami women with hugely overfilled, giant, glossy duck lips, so swollen and stiff they can barely open their mouths, long fake lashes, heavy contour makeup, long stiletto acrylic nails. Three clearly different women, not twins, and they keep their seats the whole video:
DRIVER: platinum blonde with sleek wet hair, giant pink glossy duck lips, baby-blue tail.
MIDDLE: tanned Latina with long black wet hair, giant nude glossy duck lips, gold-and-bronze tail.
PASSENGER: pale redhead with wet copper curls, giant red glossy duck lips, emerald-green tail, sly.

Layout locked for the whole video: the car is stopped at the curb; the officer stands on the sidewalk at the passenger door, looking down into the open car. The camera on his chest is about half a meter from the PASSENGER's face, with the MIDDLE one and the DRIVER right behind her, all three faces big in the frame. The officer's flashlight is in his left hand; a wrapped fish sandwich sticks out of his shirt pocket at the bottom of the frame.

Hands: the officer has only his own two hands; each mermaid has only her own two hands; no extra hands appear. There is only one seashell and one sandwich in the whole video.

Important: they never laugh and never panic; they stay bored, glamorous and offended, like this happens every night. They speak slowly, slurred and muffled, barely moving their giant lips. All three are alive and moving every second, each doing something different: no one ever freezes or stares blankly while another acts. Never gross: no spitting, no gagging.

0-3s: From the very first frame the flashlight hits all three faces, water sloshing in the cabin; the officer taps his flashlight on the top edge of the passenger door, clink clink; the PASSENGER slowly turns her face up to the camera, her giant red lips glistening, then her eyes drop to the sandwich in his pocket; the MIDDLE one shields her eyes from the flashlight with her nails; the DRIVER drums her nails on the wheel.
3-6s: The officer says in a tired voice: "License and registration." The DRIVER leans across the other two and places a big pink seashell into his open right hand with her long nails; the MIDDLE one checks her lips in the rearview mirror; the PASSENGER's emerald tail slaps her door.
6-9s: The camera tilts down to the seashell in his hand as he stares at it; at the same moment the PASSENGER's hand slides up and her nails pull the fish sandwich out of his shirt pocket.
9-12s: The officer points the flashlight at the PASSENGER: she is calmly holding the sandwich between her giant red lips; the MIDDLE one blows a slow kiss straight at the camera; the DRIVER grips the wheel and revs the engine.
12-15s: The PASSENGER's emerald tail swings up out of the water and slaps a big wave of water right at the camera; the lens is splashed with water drops, the officer stumbles back a step on the sidewalk, gasping.
15-18s: Through the wet, dripping lens: the lowrider bounces hard on its hydraulics, water sloshing out over the doors, and peels away from the curb, three tails waving over the doors.
18-20s: The officer stands soaked on the sidewalk in the flashing red and blue lights; the camera tilts down to the seashell still in his hand, then back up at the lowrider's taillights disappearing down the street, until the last second.

Sound: police radio chatter, the flashlight tapping metal, idling engine, water sloshing, the officer's tired voice and breathing, slurred muffled voices, a big splash, hydraulics squeaking, the engine roaring away, wind noise on the body camera mic. No music, no laughter.

title: 沙漠土狼的糟糕计划（30 秒）
author: @john_my07
summary: 纪录片质感混搭卡通物理的 30 秒荒野喜剧，诱饵、投石机、沙坑到仙人掌果，分段时间轴和音效写得很完整。
prompt:
DESERT MAYHEM | THE COYOTE'S TERRIBLE PLAN

Create an exactly 30-second ultra-photorealistic live-action wildlife comedy featuring an original desert coyote and a ridiculously fast roadrunner. The visuals should resemble authentic wildlife documentary footage mixed with exaggerated classic slapstick cartoon physics. Every gag must be visually clear, fast-paced, and entertaining.

FORMAT & VISUAL STYLE

16:9 cinematic widescreen, 24fps, photorealistic animals, realistic fur and feathers, natural sunlight, rich warm desert colors, detailed environments, dynamic camera angles, believable shadows, and physically expressive character animation.

CHARACTERS

THE COYOTE: A scruffy grey-brown desert coyote with oversized amber eyes, expressive eyebrows, and hilarious facial reactions. Clever but hopelessly unlucky. Stands on his hind legs when operating equipment and constantly develops overconfident plans.

THE ROADRUNNER: A small elegant desert roadrunner with speckled brown feathers, a long tail, and a distinctive crest. Extremely fast, effortlessly confident, and completely unfazed by the coyote's traps.

LOCATION

A spectacular fictional American desert landscape featuring enormous red sandstone formations, winding dusty trails, dry bushes, isolated mesas, and a narrow mountain road beneath a bright blue sky.

SEQUENCE 1 — THE BAIT (0–7s)

Wide establishing shot of the desert. The coyote stands beside a freshly constructed wooden roadside food stand displaying a giant juicy watermelon. He rubs his paws together and hides behind a cactus.

A roadrunner appears in the distance and approaches at incredible speed.

Just as the bird reaches the watermelon, it casually grabs it without stopping, leaving the coyote staring in disbelief.

The coyote looks down at the empty stand, then slowly turns toward the camera with an offended expression.

Sound: Playful orchestral pizzicato, wooden stand creaking, rapid running whoosh, a cheeky bird chirp, and a comedic disappointed trombone.

SEQUENCE 2 — THE CATAPULT DISASTER (7–14s)

The frustrated coyote constructs an enormous homemade wooden catapult on a rocky hillside. He loads himself into its launching seat, pulls a rope, and prepares to launch across the road to intercept the roadrunner.

Extreme close-up of his confident grin.

He releases the mechanism.

The catapult launches him straight upward instead of forward. He disappears above the frame, followed by a brief silence.

Cut to a wide shot: he drops directly into a giant prickly desert bush, with only his legs sticking out.

Meanwhile, the roadrunner casually walks past in the background.

Sound: Wooden mechanism creaks, rope snap, powerful launch BOING, wind whistle, followed by a massive bush impact and tiny cactus rattles.

SEQUENCE 3 — THE SAND TRAP (14–22s)

The coyote emerges covered in cactus needles, furious but determined.

He sets up a cleverly disguised sand trap on a narrow dirt trail, covering a large pit with dry branches and sand. He hides behind a boulder and watches.

The roadrunner approaches, notices the suspicious ground, and effortlessly jumps over the trap.

The coyote jumps out excitedly to celebrate, but accidentally steps onto his own fragile covering.

The ground collapses beneath him. He disappears into the pit, leaving a cloud of dust and two paws sticking out.

The roadrunner pauses, tilts its head, and gives a smug little chirp.

Sound: Sneaky orchestral strings, sand brushing, quick bird footsteps, a springy jump whoosh, sudden cracking branches, deep dirt collapse, and a comic whistle.

SEQUENCE 4 — THE FINAL REVENGE (22–30s)

The dusty coyote climbs out of the pit and spots a huge round cactus fruit balanced on a steep rocky slope.

A wicked grin slowly spreads across his face.

He carefully positions himself behind the fruit and gives it a powerful push toward the dirt trail, expecting it to roll directly into the approaching roadrunner.

But the fruit hits a small rock, changes direction, and starts rolling straight back toward him.

The coyote's eyes widen.

Quick tracking shot as the enormous fruit barrels downhill, knocking him into a spectacular tumble through the dust.

Final wide cinematic shot: the coyote lies sprawled on the desert trail, covered in cactus spines, while the roadrunner calmly stands beside him, looks directly at the camera, gives its signature cheeky call, and vanishes in a cloud of dust.

End on a brief comedic freeze-frame.

Sound: Dramatic villain brass sting, rolling rumble, accelerating whoosh, several exaggerated impacts, a final deep THUD, sad trombone, and a cheeky bird call.

AUDIO & SOUND DESIGN

Use continuous energetic cartoon-style orchestral comedy music throughout, with pizzicato strings, playful brass, percussion, and perfectly timed musical pauses.

Layer crisp environmental sounds, desert wind, running footsteps, wooden creaks, spring-loaded mechanisms, exaggerated boings, slide whistles, deep impact thuds, and fast-motion whooshes.

No spoken dialogue, no narration, no subtitles, and no text overlays.

IMPORTANT CONSISTENCY RULES

- Maintain identical coyote and roadrunner appearances throughout all four sequences.
- Preserve realistic animal fur, feathers, anatomy, and natural desert lighting.
- Use exaggerated cartoon physics only for comedic impacts and reactions.
- Keep the roadrunner consistently calm, fast, and effortlessly successful.
- Make every action readable with clear cause-and-effect.
- Use dynamic cinematic editing with seamless continuity between shots.
- Avoid character morphing, duplicate animals, distorted anatomy, artificial CGI appearance, and unnecessary slow motion.
- Prioritize sharp, detailed visuals and expressive facial animation.

title: 雨中首尔恋爱短片（30 秒）

title: 天桥断电 THE SKYBRIDGE（30 秒）
author: @ChillaiKalan__
summary: 暴雨夜玻璃天桥上的六镜动作惊悚，结尾留了「黑灯不是全部」的悬念，分镜和物理约束清楚。
prompt:
Create a 30-second photorealistic Hollywood action-thriller sequence titled "THE SKYBRIDGE".

FORMAT:
Vertical 9:16, 4K, 60 FPS.
Exactly 30 seconds.
Six shots, exactly 5 seconds each.
Exactly five hard cinematic cuts.

CHARACTER LOCK:
Use @Image1 as the exact reference for BLACK ROSE.
Preserve her original face, facial proportions, natural skin texture, messy black updo, black fitted clothing, black floral embroidered outerwear, necklaces and heeled lace-up boots.
No beautification, no face changes, no outfit changes.
Her expression is calm, rebellious and controlled.
Her voice is low, confident and natural.

LOCATION:
A glass skybridge connecting two skyscrapers, hundreds of metres above a modern city at night.
Heavy rain strikes the glass walls.
Lightning illuminates the skyline.
The bridge has a polished reflective floor, steel support beams, emergency lights and a central maintenance hatch.
A frightened male engineer carries a small emergency access key.

EXACTLY THREE ATTACKERS:
Attacker 1: broad build, dark navy suit, positioned near the elevator entrance.
Attacker 2: athletic build, grey tactical shirt, positioned beside the central support beam.
Attacker 3: tall, black coat, positioned near the far exit.
Keep all appearances consistent.

SHOT 1 — 00:00–00:05
Start with a dramatic exterior aerial shot revealing the glass skybridge suspended between two skyscrapers.
The camera moves toward the glass and passes inside.
BLACK ROSE stands beside the engineer.
The city lights suddenly go dark.
Emergency red lighting activates.
Three men emerge from opposite ends of the bridge.
A deep electrical hum fills the space.

SHOT 2 — 00:05–00:10
Attacker 1 approaches and grabs for the engineer's access key.
BLACK ROSE steps between them, catches his reaching arm and performs a sharp wrist control followed by a compact shoulder throw.
He lands hard but safely on the padded floor section.
The engineer retreats behind a steel support beam.
Camera tracks low and close.

SHOT 3 — 00:10–00:15
Attacker 2 rushes forward.
BLACK ROSE pivots around a support beam, avoids his first strike and uses a fast Savate-style kick to disrupt his balance.
She follows with a controlled forearm strike.
He stumbles into the padded side wall and drops to one knee.
A 0.25-second micro slow-motion moment captures the impact, then immediately return to real-time.
The glass remains intact.

SHOT 4 — 00:15–00:20
Attacker 3 charges from the far exit.
BLACK ROSE moves laterally as he passes, catches his momentum and executes a Judo-style foot sweep.
He loses balance and slides across the floor, stopping safely before the glass wall.
Camera follows his movement with a controlled tracking shot.
Do not show the bridge breaking.

SHOT 5 — 00:20–00:25
The engineer reaches the maintenance hatch and inserts the emergency access key.
BLACK ROSE watches the three defeated attackers behind her.
A sudden vibration shakes the bridge.
She looks toward the far skyscraper.
A huge dark shape moves behind the clouds.
She says quietly:
"That wasn't the blackout."

SHOT 6 — 00:25–00:30
The camera pulls outside the skybridge.
Both skyscrapers are dark, except for one illuminated floor.
Through the glass, BLACK ROSE and the engineer look upward.
A second bridge, far above them, suddenly lights up.
A human silhouette stands inside it.
Cut to black.

ACTION PHYSICS:
Every movement must show contact, momentum, recoil and believable balance loss.
No teleportation, floating bodies or impossible acrobatics.
Exactly three attackers, never duplicated.
Preserve the skybridge geography and character positions.
No glass explosions or unrealistic structural damage.

AUDIO:
Heavy rain against glass, distant thunder, electrical hum, emergency alarms, footsteps, realistic clothing movement and non-graphic impact sounds.
Natural dialogue only.
No background music, no subtitles, no text overlays.

VISUAL STYLE:
Premium Hollywood sci-fi action thriller.
Photorealistic city lights, dramatic reflections, realistic rain, cinematic lens depth, controlled camera movement and high-contrast practical lighting.
No blood or gore.

title: 转学生以一敌三（30 秒）
author: @saniaspeaks_
summary: 韩式校园动作短剧，教室到走廊的冲突和台词都按时间轴写好，人物设定比较完整。
prompt:
THE TRANSFER STUDENT — KOREA

Create an exactly 30-second ultra-realistic live-action Korean school action drama featuring real actors, natural lighting and realistic martial arts choreography.

MAIN CHARACTERS — STRICT CONSISTENCY

- Transfer Student: A quiet 17-year-old Korean girl with shoulder-length straight black hair and soft bangs. She wears a white shirt, navy blazer, dark ribbon tie, navy pleated skirt, white socks and black shoes. She carries a black schoolbag.
- Victim: A shy 17-year-old Korean boy with short black hair, white shirt and navy trousers.
- Three Bullies: Three distinct Korean male students aged 17–18, wearing untidy white shirts, loosened ties and navy trousers.
- Teacher: A Korean female teacher in her early 30s.

Keep every character's face, hairstyle, clothing and appearance consistent throughout.

SCENE 1 — NEW TRANSFER STUDENT (0–6s)

Inside a modern Korean classroom, the teacher introduces the new girl. She enters with her black schoolbag, bows politely and says, "안녕하세요." Students watch curiously as she takes a seat near the window.

SCENE 2 — BULLYING (6–12s)

During lunch break, three bullies surround a shy boy in the school corridor. One pushes him, another steals his notebook, and the third blocks his way. The notebook falls to the floor as the boy bends to retrieve it.

SCENE 3 — INTERVENTION (12–17s)

The transfer student notices the bullying, approaches and picks up the notebook. She returns it to the boy and firmly says, "그만해!" The main bully laughs and pushes her shoulder. She steps back, maintains her balance and gives him a determined look.

SCENE 4 — MARTIAL ARTS REVEAL (17–25s)

The bully throws a punch. She dodges, blocks his next strike, redirects his arm and brings him down onto his knees. The second bully grabs her blazer, but she blocks his arm and pushes him backwards into the lockers. The third bully approaches but hesitates. She takes a defensive stance as all three stop advancing.

Show the complete choreography with realistic contact, balance, movement and momentum. No flying bodies, superhero moves or excessive violence.

SCENE 5 — FINAL TWIST (25–30s)

The bullies step back in disbelief. The victim stands up and asks, "너 누구야?" She calmly adjusts her blazer, picks up her schoolbag and replies, "그냥 전학생이야." She walks confidently down the corridor as the boy watches in amazement.

VISUAL STYLE: Photorealistic 4K live-action Korean action drama, authentic school locations, natural late-afternoon lighting, realistic skin, facial expressions, body movement and handheld cinematography. Use medium-wide shots to clearly show the fight.

AUDIO: Natural classroom ambience, Korean dialogue synchronized with lip movements, footsteps, notebook drop, locker sounds and realistic fight impacts. No narration or background music.

STRICT RULES: Preserve all character identities, uniforms, props and locations. Keep the exact scene order and show every important action. No scene skipping, face changes, duplicate characters, disappearing people, outfit changes, distorted hands, artificial transitions or cartoon effects.

title: 懒散周日与猫咪（30 秒）
author: @Ciri_ai
summary: 手持纪录片质感的 12 镜生活切片：赖床、购物、猫咪抢手机、门铃收尾，对白和同期声很细。
prompt:
Montage, multi-shot candid observational footage. Do not use a single camera angle or continuous take. Handheld documentary style with the feeling of accidental real-life capture. Slightly imperfect framing, subtle handheld shake, tiny reframing adjustments, gentle exposure breathing, and autofocus that settles half a beat late. Realistic skin texture, soft late-morning window light with dust drifting in the sunbeams, film grain, shallow depth of field. Relaxed breathing, natural blinking, restrained and authentic performance. Total of 12 shots, 30 seconds.

The woman from <<<image_1>>>  is wearing a matching cotton pajama set: a scoop-neck sleeveless top and loose shorts in the same fabric and design. Barefoot, hair messy from sleep. It is a lazy Sunday and her bedroom is lived-in: tangled blanket, a half-drunk mug, clothes draped over a chair, a laundry basket by the wall. She wakes late, scrolls a mobile shopping page on a black smartphone, gets interrupted by her house cat, takes a call from a friend, starts tidying the room while chatting, and is finally interrupted by the doorbell as a late punchline.

Shot 1 (0–2s):
Close on her face half buried in the pillow, eyes barely open, morning light across her cheek. She fumbles for the phone on the mattress without looking. She mumbles in Korean: "아… 몇 시야, 지금." ("Ah... what time is it now."). Lips sync naturally. Camera low on the pillow, slightly out of focus, then settles.

Shot 2 (2–5s):
She rolls onto her stomach, bare feet swaying behind her, thumb scrolling a shopping page. She frowns, thinking. She mutters: "아, 뭐 살랬더라…" ("Ah... what was I going to buy again?"). Low handheld camera glides along the mattress edge, bedding partially blurring the foreground.

Shot 3 (5–7s):
The house cat jumps onto the bed, compressing the blanket, and walks straight across her phone screen. Slight camera jolt from the impact, then a quick reframe to an over-the-shoulder view including her face, hands, phone and the cat's tail covering the screen.

Shot 4 (7–10s):
She pushes the cat's tail aside, then gives in and strokes it from forehead to shoulders. In a soft, teasing tone: "야, 비켜봐. 우리 애기 왔어?" ("Hey, move over. Did my baby come?"). The camera pushes in through the cat's blurred foreground toward her face and hand. The cat flops down on the phone.

Shot 5 (10–12s):
She lifts the cat off the phone, laughing quietly, and holds it up. The cat dangles with a flat, unimpressed expression. The camera tilts slightly and reframes late. She puts the cat down, and it immediately starts kneading the blanket.

Shot 6 (12–14s):
A friend's ringtone sounds. She glances at the screen, confirms the caller, swipes to answer and holds the phone to her ear. Camera moves in a loose semicircle from a slightly tilted overhead angle, capturing the whole answering motion.

Shot 7 (14–17s):
Her friend begins talking through the phone. She sits up cross-legged against the headboard and responds first with confusion, then disbelief: "어, 왜? 진짜? 거짓말." ("Huh? Why? Really? You're kidding."). Immediately afterward she bursts into natural laughter. Close handheld side angle keeps her phone and profile on the same focal plane.

Shot 8 (17–20s):
Still laughing, she cradles the phone with her shoulder and starts tidying one-handed: gathers the half-drunk mug, tosses a shirt toward the laundry basket and misses. The cat watches. Camera follows at waist height with a slight lag, catching her bare feet on the floor.

Shot 9 (20–23s):
She drags the blanket straight, and the cat, still on it, slides along with it, offended. She laughs again and says to her friend: "잠깐만, 나 지금 방 치우는 중이야." ("Wait, I'm cleaning my room right now."). Camera over her shoulder, a quick whip reframe to the cat's face, then back to her.

Shot 10 (23–26s):
She plops back on the bed with the phone, the room now only half tidy. The friend says something funny, and she covers her mouth, wheezing with laughter, shoulders shaking. The cat curls up on the pillow beside her. Close, slightly shaky shot that drifts across her face and the cat's ear.

Shot 11 (26–28s):
A clear doorbell cuts through the laughter. Both she and the cat freeze and turn toward the bedroom door. She mouths, "아…" and realizes. The camera reacts a fraction too late, briefly turning toward the door before correcting back to her face.

Shot 12 (28–30s):
Still on the phone, she hurriedly says: "어, 나 밥 왔다. 끊어. 아, 근데 나 아직 안 씻었다." ("Oh, my food's here. I'll hang up. Wait, I haven't even washed yet."). She ends the call with her thumb, scrambles off the bed, and pats down her messy hair while walking toward the door, the cat trotting behind her through the blankets. Camera slides low beneath her elbow and tilts upward as she stands in one continuous motion.

Sound:
No music. Only raw production sound: bedding rustling, quiet breathing, a groggy morning exhale, finger taps and scrolls on the phone, the soft thud of the cat landing on the bed, one or two natural meows, faint purring, a single short incoming ringtone, call connection tone, the friend's voice faintly through the phone, the woman's Korean lines with accurate lip sync, genuine brief laughter, a mug clinking, a shirt thrown into a basket, one clear doorbell, the tap ending the call, bare footsteps and soft cat footsteps. No subtitles, no on-screen text, no logo, no watermark. Never render a reference sheet or duplicate the subject.
